title: [Mouse Without Borders] settings.json sharing violation causes security keys to diverge between PCs → control channel (TCP 15100) fails, keyboard only works one way with "ding" error
summary: Mouse Without Borders settings writes reportedly fail during concurrent access, leaving the two paired PCs with divergent security keys and a one-way keyboard control channel.
next_action: Coordinate the shared settings-persistence fix with issue #51682 and verify that the reported pairing failure is covered by the same correction.

judgment.rationale: The supplied report and diagnostic archive describe settings-file sharing failures alongside key divergence and control-channel handshake failures. Open issue #51682 documents the same incompatible settings-file sharing behavior with independent Process Monitor evidence. This report adds a distinct user-visible symptom but points to the same persistence defect, so the fix should be coordinated with #51682 rather than treated as a separate networking failure.

judgment.recommended_action: Use #51682 as the primary tracking issue for a cross-process-safe settings persistence fix, and verify that the fix prevents security-key divergence and restores reliable control-channel pairing.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported persistence failure matches the shared settings-file contention documented in #51682. The correction should be implemented and tracked with that issue, not as a separate networking workaround.

proposed_fixes.title: Make Mouse Without Borders settings persistence safe under concurrent access
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Settings UI, Quick Access, and Mouse Without Borders can access the same settings file concurrently with incompatible file-sharing behavior. A failed write can leave the in-memory and persisted pairing keys out of sync; the peer then rejects the control-channel handshake.
plan: Coordinate implementation with issue #51682 and trace the settings read/write paths used by Settings UI, Quick Access, and Mouse Without Borders.
Use a cross-process-safe persistence strategy that permits compatible reads, serializes competing updates, and replaces the settings file atomically without dropping unrelated settings.
Add deterministic contention coverage for concurrent readers and writers, including preservation of the security key and valid settings JSON.
Verify that reconnecting two paired PCs under the reported conditions keeps both keys consistent and establishes bidirectional keyboard control.
verification: Exercise concurrent Settings UI, Quick Access, and Mouse Without Borders settings access while triggering reconnects; verify that no settings write is lost or rejected.
Restart both paired PCs and verify that their security keys remain consistent and the TCP 15100 control channel stays established.
Run the focused settings persistence tests and Mouse Without Borders regression tests on the corrected build.

confidence.rationale: The supplied diagnostics describe settings sharing failures at the same time as key divergence, and #51682 independently establishes the incompatible sharing behavior. The exact user-visible handshake symptom is new, but the underlying persistence defect is directly supported.

reproduce.title: Verify Mouse Without Borders settings persistence during reconnect
prerequisites: Two Windows PCs paired with Mouse Without Borders.
The PowerToys Settings window or Quick Access available while Mouse Without Borders is running.
setup: Confirm that mouse and keyboard transfer work in both directions before testing.
steps: Keep Settings or Quick Access open while Mouse Without Borders is active.
Trigger a reconnect or allow the peer to reconnect.
Check whether either PC reports a settings write failure or whether the pairing keys diverge.
Restart both PCs and verify the control channel and keyboard transfer in both directions.
reproduce.expected_result: Settings persist without sharing failures, both PCs retain consistent pairing keys, and keyboard input works in both directions after reconnect and restart.
